analysis: The code snippet calls Class.forName(className) with an unvalidated input string. The method's documentation declares three exception types: LinkageError, ExceptionInInitializerError, and ClassNotFoundException. The surrounding code does not perform any checks on className (e.g., verifying it is a valid binary name or ensuring the class is loadable). The only handling is a catch for ClassNotFoundException, which does not prevent the exception from being thrown. Therefore, all three exceptions are not avoided in this context.
remark: LinkageError can be triggered if the class's linkage fails (e.g., missing dependencies, incompatible version). ExceptionInInitializerError occurs when the static initializer of the class throws an exception. ClassNotFoundException happens if the class cannot be found by the given name on the classpath. All are possible because the input 'className' is not validated or sanitized before the call.
